newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia manufacturers output seen up in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia manufacturers output seen up in 2nd half.

text.p: Malaysia's manufacturing sector is expected to see 9.7 percent growth in total output in the last half of 1996 from the first half of the year, the national Bernama news agency reported.
Sales volume for the sector was expected to grow 8.8 percent for the second half over the six months, it said.

Bernama quoted a Malaysian Industrial Development Authority (MIDA) report as saying the sector expected double-digit gains in production and sales, including rubber, wood, electronics machinery and transport equipment.
In the first half of 1996, the sector recorded increases of 2.5 percent and 5.1 percent in aggregate output and sales, respectively, over the last half of 1995, MIDA said.

While the output of electrical products was expected to be hurt by a seasonal production decline, the electronics industry output was projected to grow by 11.5 percent and sales demand to rise by 13.8 percent in the last half of 1996.
The electronics industry worldwide was hit earlier this year by an oversupply in components, particularly in memory chips, leading to sharp declines in component prices.

MIDA said employment was projected to rise by 3.5 percent in the last six months of 1996 from the first half, with higher recruitment of new workers expected in all industries surveyed except for textile products.
Overall salary expenditure was forecast to grow by 10.8 percent during the period.
The survey concluded that the last six months of 1996 would see a 5.2 percent increase in plant and machinery investments from the first half.
